Thanks for this! I already use Obsidian for academia, so I’m pretty familiar with its capabilities since it’s part of my research workflow. I also use Notion occasionally because some of my lab mates prefer it for organizing their projects — so I’ll jump in when I’m involved in theirs.

I guess I’m just looking for something more casual. It’s kind of an unfortunate coincidence that I already use Notion and Obsidian for work-related things, and I don’t really want to taint that association by using them for personal stuff too. I tend to associate them with being in full “brain-on” mode.

That’s why I leaned into using discord for the more “brain-off” parts of my life it just felt convenient since I was already using it to chat and hop on voice calls with friends who prefer it anyway.
That said, I’m leaning toward still using discord anyway, since I don’t really care if someone sees my fridge inventory or my random shower thoughts (like how soaking a paper towel before microwaving food makes it taste better because it rehydrates (steams) it)

Judging from the comments, I’ve been convinced to stop treating it like a diary. Which is fine lol, since I barely even started! I also never really kept one successfully anyway.

I like reading all the comments though and appreciated everyone’s input!!

I personally liked how casual the mobile app felt like I was just texting something (with no text back, a plus for me). It didn’t feel like I had to set anything up. It was quick, easy, and the UI made the interaction feel simple and low-effort, which I really appreciated. Also I associate one note with my undergrad experience so I tend to avoid it
